title: The Psalm of the Crucifixion
hint: David describes Christ's suffering 1,000 years before the cross
intro: Psalm 22 is the most detailed Messianic prophecy about the crucifixion. David describes sufferings he himself never experienced—but which Jesus fulfilled literally. Jesus quoted the opening words of this psalm from the cross.

items.title: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
items.note: Quoted by Jesus on the cross (Matt 27:46)

items.title: Poured out like water
items.note: Describes the physical suffering of crucifixion

items.title: My tongue sticks to my jaws
Hands and feet pierced
items.note: Crucifixion—1,000 years before the Romans used it!

items.title: All my bones can be counted
They divide my garments among them
All the ends of the earth

footer.title: The Suffering Messiah
footer.content: Psalm 22 proves that the crucifixion was in God's plan from eternity. David saw through the Spirit what the Messiah would suffer—over 1,000 years before it happened. The psalm ends in victory: "He has done it!" (v.31)—echoing Jesus' words, "It is finished!"
